description:
FOUND s473t5e (#1501 round 6, `re/` CHECK 2) as the SECOND of t/re/reg_posixcc.t's
two facts, and the one that outlives the POSIX-class fix (#1501 round 6 FIX 1,
commit "a POSIX bracket class and `[:^class:]` are COMPLEMENTS").

cl-ppcre's `map-char-to-special-char-class` (cl/vendor/cl-ppcre/lexer.lisp:41)
answers for exactly SIX escapes -- `\d \D \w \W \s \S` -- and `\p`/`\P` through
the property resolver.  `\h \H \v \V \R` are not in it, so the backslash falls
through to `handle-char` and the pattern matches the LETTER:

  PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl), one code point per row, `1` = matched:
    cp       perl h/H/v/V     PCL h/H/v/V
    0x0009   1 0 0 1          0 0 0 0
    0x0020   1 0 0 1          0 0 0 0
    0x000A   0 1 1 0          0 0 0 0
    0x000B   0 1 1 0          0 0 0 0
    0x0068   0 1 0 1          1 0 0 0     <- 'h' matches /\h/
    0x0048   0 1 0 1          0 1 0 0     <- 'H' matches /\H/
    0x00A0   1 0 0 1          0 0 0 0
    0x2028   0 1 1 0          0 0 0 0

So `/\h+/` (a common CPAN idiom for "horizontal whitespace") matches a run of
the letter h and nothing else.  SILENT WRONG, no diagnostic.

ROWS BEHIND IT: t/re/reg_posixcc.t, after FIX 1, is DIFF 1544/1016 (was
1544/7646).  All 1,016 remaining diverging rows are the file's
`ok(($chr =~ /$yes/) != ($chr =~ /$no/), "$type: chr(N) isn't both $yes and $no")`
assertions for the `\h`/`\H` and `\v`/`\V` pairs: 2 pairs x 256 code points x 2
string types = 1,024, of which 8 accidentally agree.  The blessed baseline
carries the first 500 (the runner's per-file cap on PAIRED diverging rows,
`tools/run-perl-suite.pl:913`); the other 516 exist and are TRUNCATED out.

perl's sets (perlrecharclass), which the fix must emit:
  \h  [\t\x20\xA0\x{1680}\x{2000}-\x{200A}\x{202F}\x{205F}\x{3000}]
  \v  [\n\x0B\f\r\x{85}\x{2028}\x{2029}]
  \H  \V  the complements
  \R  (?:\r\n|[\n\x0B\f\r\x{85}\x{2028}\x{2029}])   -- NOT usable in a class

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, and what the shape is.  The rewrite lives in
`perl-regex-to-ppcre` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), a chain of context-free
`regex-replace-all` passes.  `\h` needs `[...]` OUTSIDE a bracket class and a
bare range list INSIDE one (`/[$yes]/` with `$yes = "\\h"` is exactly what
reg_posixcc.t writes), and `\H` inside a class needs the COMPLEMENT ranges,
since a class's own `^` applies to the whole class.  So the pass must know
whether each occurrence is inside a bracket class -- one forward scan tracking
`in-class`, handling `\[`, a literal `]` as a class's first character, and the
`[:name:]` inner brackets (which the POSIX pass has already removed by then).
About 35-40 lines, one function, and it is a NEW mechanism in that chain --
which is why s473t5e shipped the POSIX half (no context needed: `[:name:]`
only ever occurs inside a class) and filed this one.

The complement machinery it needs ALREADY EXISTS as of FIX 1:
`+p-posix-class-ranges+` / `%pcl-posix-complement` / `%pcl-regex-class-char`
(which backslash-escapes the five characters that would otherwise end or
reshape a class).  Give `\h` and `\v` entries in a sibling table of the same
shape and the rendering is free; the only new code is the in-class scan.

ACCEPTANCE BAR: the 8-row probe above identical to perl; t/re/reg_posixcc.t
1544/1016 -> 2560/0 (the file then FULLY PASSES, and its 7,130 blessed rows
leave `baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` by EDIT); a `Pl/t/posix-class-01.t` row
of the same shape as its row 2 (the complement property) extended to \h/\v;
and the case the change would BREAK probed -- a pattern using `\h` where the
program means the letter h is not a thing, but `[\v]` vs `\v` inside `(?x:...)`
and `\R` at top level are (perl's `\R` is not allowed in a class at all:
"\R cannot be used inside a character class").

=== DONE (s484c) ===
SHIPPED 2026-09-14, commit "s484c member 2 (#1713): \h \H \v \V \R are not
letters" (runtime-only; no generation bump).

cl-ppcre's map-char-to-special-char-class answers for exactly six escapes, so
\h fell through to the LETTER h.  perl's two sets are Unicode (probed code
point by code point over 0..0x11000) and \h/\H, \v/\V are complements
everywhere.  ONE forward scan %pcl-expand-hv-escapes, after the \Q and POSIX
passes, POSITION-SENSITIVE: outside a bracket class \h is a class of its own
and \H its negated twin; inside one it contributes bare ranges and \H the
COMPLEMENT ranges (a class's own ^ applies to the whole class).  \R is the
linebreak atom at top level and is left alone inside a class -- which IS perl's
answer there: an unrecognised escape, warned about and passed through as the
letter R (probed; the docstring that claimed perl rejects it was corrected in
the batch's last commit).  Rule 12: a letter with no range table now dies.

MEASURED: the task's 8-row code-point probe plus the class/complement/breaking
rows identical to perl.  t/re/reg_posixcc.t 1544/1016 -> 2560/0 -- the file
FULLY PASSES, and its 500 blessed fail rows left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv
by EDIT.  t/re/pat_advanced.t 951/729 -> 1258/422 (base extraction 958/722
parallel AND serial; 195 of the 207 disappearing failures name \h \v \H \V or
HORIZWS).  Guard Pl/t/posix-class-01.t 3 -> 5 rows, inverse-verified.  ir-spec
Â§10-esc is normative.
subject: `\h` `\H` `\v` `\V` (and `\R`) are LITERAL h/H/v/V in every pattern -- cl-ppcre has only \d\D\w\W\s\S, so `/\h+/` matches the letter h: SILENT WRONG in real code, and 1,016 rows of t/re/reg_posixcc.t
